parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Use a correct isosceles-triangle method with their $A,B,C$, e.g. $\theta=2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac52\right)$, or $\sin(\theta/2)=5/\sqrt{29}$, or $\cos(\theta/2)=2/\sqrt{29}$, or $\theta=\pi-2\tan^{-1}(2/5)$, or the cosine rule $10^2=29+29-2\sqrt{29}\sqrt{29}\cos\theta$, giving $\cos\theta=-21/29$. M1. Note: $\tan\theta=5/2$ scores 0/2 unless the angle is doubled; using $r=29$ scores 0/2. $\theta=2.38$. A1 AWRT; final $136.4^\circ$ scores max 1/2; ignore degree symbol if present. Alternative: use $\tan\theta=(m_2-m_1)/(1+m_1m_2)$ with the gradients of their $AC$ and $BC$ of the required form, then $\theta=2.38$. M1A1 AWRT. Total: 2.

parts.label: (c)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Identify $AC=BC=\sqrt{5^2+2^2}=\sqrt{29}$ (condone $5.4$). B1; may have been found earlier but must be seen in part (c). Use a correct sector formula with their identified radius and their $2\pi-\theta$ or $\theta$, e.g. large sector $=\frac12(\sqrt{29})^2(2\pi-\theta)$ or small sector $=\frac12(\sqrt{29})^2\theta$. M1; may be embedded. Use a correct triangle formula with their radius and angle, e.g. $\frac12(\sqrt{29})^2\sin\theta$ or $\frac12(10)(2)=10$. M1; may be embedded. Larger segment area $=66.6$. A1 AWRT; equivalently circle area minus smaller segment, $29\pi-34.52+10$. Total: 4.
